director.chapterArc: A tense confrontation where Wyck Tanner forces Rook to acknowledge a secret plan; Milo voices his fear of being bait; Rook admits the truth but delays full disclosure until he is ready, shifting the group dynamic from suspicion to protective solidarity.
director.restraintNote: Maintain Toren's analytical distance throughout. Do not dramatize Wyck's accusation or Milo's panic as hysterical outbursts; they are factual observations of a broken system. Rook's admission must feel like a heavy, reluctant confession, not an emotional release. The ending should settle into quiet vigilance.

cues.delivery: Wyck's request is delivered with flat, factual urgency; Senna's response carries a dry, protective warmth that acknowledges the weight of his need without softening it.
cues.from: "I know. I want you awake and sitting up." Wyck was lying propped on his elbow with his back against the rail, in the place he had lived for eight days. "I put a thing off once because you were asleep. I'm not putting it off twice. So I'd rather you were there and heard it than be told about it afterward by one of them."
cues.through: "No," she agreed. "It's better than nice. Prop that blanket behind me at the halt and I'll do the rest."
cues.reason: Establishes Wyck's vulnerability and Senna's acceptance before the confrontation begins.

cues.delivery: Wyck speaks with a rhythmic, counting cadence; his voice is flat and precise as he lists the group's status to establish authority before speaking.
cues.from: "Three things first, in that order." Wyck's voice was the one he used for reading out a number. "There's six of us. Two are mending. We're going north."
cues.through: "I'm not being clever. I'm doing it the way he taught us, because I want him to know I'm doing it on purpose and not because I lost my temper." Wyck did not look away from Rook once. "I've had this ready for eight days and I've rebuilt it about forty times. What's left of it is short."
cues.reason: Sets up Wyck's methodical approach to the confrontation.

cues.delivery: Wyck recites Rook's past teachings with a flat, accusatory rhythm; the subtext is that Rook has been lying by omission. The delivery must remain controlled to avoid sounding like an angry outburst.
cues.from: "Twenty-five days ago you told us we weren't going to learn to fight." He said it the way he said everything, flat, in order, without any heat on it. "You said it at a north gate at first light. You said fighting takes years and we don't have years and three of us haven't got anything to fight with. You said we were going to learn not to be standing where the thing is. I can say the whole of it back if you want it."
cues.through: "So." Wyck took a breath. It caught on the ribs, and he went on through it. "A fortnight of a thing that can't change its mind, and then, suddenly, everything about a thing that can. That's not a course. That's not somebody teaching four children how to stay alive on a road. That's a man getting something ready."
cues.reason: The core accusation of hypocrisy requires precise, unemotional articulation.

cues.delivery: Milo's question 'Are we bait?' is delivered with a voice that has gone cold and factual; the panic is internalized in his physical description rather than vocal strain.
cues.through: "Because I was," Milo said. "That's the thing. Eight days ago I stood in a hole in a bridge and made a light on purpose, so that a thing would come at me instead of at somebody else. And it worked. And you told me never to do it again and then you told me it worked." He wiped his face with his wrist, angrily, the way he did. "And I've been fine about that. I've been completely fine about it. And then last night you taught us all how to be close to a man and I lay down and thought — right, so what's the light for, then. On a road. With people on it."
cues.reason: The horror of Milo's realization must land as a quiet shock.

cues.delivery: Rook moves quickly but speaks with a sudden loss of his usual flatness; the denial is personal and urgent, breaking his standard cadence to reassure Milo.
cues.through: "I said it worked. It did work. It also should not have been available to you, and the reason it was available to you is that I was in the wrong place." Rook stood up. "Ask me the question again in a year and I will give you the same answer in the same words, because it will still be true. Nobody in this group is bait. If I ever decide otherwise I will say it out loud to your face beforehand, and you can tell me what you think of it."
cues.reason: Marks Rook's rare moment of emotional vulnerability.

cues.delivery: Rook delivers the line 'There is an account' with a flat, bill-reading cadence; the subtext is that he has been carrying this burden alone for years.
cues.through: "That's —" Toren heard his own voice and did not much like it. "That's the same as no."
cues.reason: The revelation of the secret must feel like a heavy fact being stated.

cues.delivery: Rook explains his decision to build something in them without their knowledge; the delivery is weary and resigned, acknowledging a flaw in his method.
cues.from: "There's one more thing," he said, "and it's the part I actually owe you. I'd rather not say it, which is generally how I know."
cues.through: "Because I did not want to be argued with, and because I have done it that way for eleven years, and because it is exactly the same thing I did to Wyck at a lock flight and got him three broken ribs for." Rook's voice did not change by one degree. "I have had that pointed out to me once this month. I would rather not need it twice."

cues.delivery: Toren's internal monologue shifts to a reflective, observational tone; the realization of their collective choice is delivered with quiet clarity.
cues.from: They went at half past one and made eight miles before the light went, and the strange thing about the afternoon was how ordinary it was.
cues.through: He could not decide whether it was the best thing they had ever done or a thing that people who had been drilled for twenty-six days would do without noticing.
cues.reason: Signals the shift from confrontation to group solidarity.

pauses.after: "No," she agreed. "It's better than nice. Prop that blanket behind me at the halt and I'll do the rest."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and transition from Senna's acceptance to Wyck's action.
Completed thought; pause for the weight of Wyck's agreement before he begins his list.

pauses.before: That's a man getting something ready.
pauses.reason: Emphasizes the core realization that Rook is preparing them for something specific.

pauses.after: "And I'd like to know what for," Wyck said. "Not because I'm owed it. I said that at Coldharbour. I meant it, and I still mean it. I'd like to know because I'm in it, and because I said yes to nothing, and because there was a day at a sheep-fold when I stood in front of a boy and told him I'd rather say no myself than have somebody say it on my behalf." He stopped. "That's the whole of it. What am I standing in a line for."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on the accusation 'What am I standing in a line for.' Allow silence to let the question hang.

pauses.after: Milo looked at his own boots for a second. When he got it out, he got it out all at once, in the voice of somebody putting a hand into cold water.
pauses.reason: Pause before Milo's devastatingly simple question; build tension.
Isolates Milo's fear as the central question of the scene.

pauses.after: "Because I was," Milo said. "That's the thing. Eight days ago I stood in a hole in a bridge and made a light on purpose, so that a thing would come at me instead of at somebody else. And it worked. And you told me never to do it again and then you told me it worked." He wiped his face with his wrist, angrily, the way he did. "And I've been fine about that. I've been completely fine about it. And then last night you taught us all how to be close to a man and I lay down and thought — right, so what's the light for, then. On a road. With people on it."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on the explanation of why he was baited. Allow Toren to process the revelation.

pauses.after: "Right." Rook walked back to where he had been standing, which was a thing Toren noticed — he put himself back at eleven feet, in the open, where everybody could see his hands. "Then here's the not-yet. I'll do it in order. I'd ask all of you not to talk in the middle of it, because I'm only going to get through it once.
pauses.reason: Completed thought; pause before Rook reveals the account exists.
Prepares for Rook's admission of a hidden burden.

pauses.after: "It is not the same as no and you know the difference, because you have been marking the difference for a fortnight." Rook's head came round. "Ask me how many times I have said no to a question of that shape since the rock cut."
pauses.reason: Major emotional landing on 'Eleven. And this is the twelfth.' Let the count sink in.
Emphasizes Dessa's challenge to Rook's secrecy.

pauses.after: "Because I did not want to be argued with, and because I have done it that way for eleven years, and because it is exactly the same thing I did to Wyck at a lock flight and got him three broken ribs for." Rook's voice did not change by one degree. "I have had that pointed out to me once this month. I would rather not need it twice."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset; pause after Rook's explanation of his method before Wyck responds.
Highlights Wyck's demand for the final piece of truth before he accepts waiting.

pauses.after: Milo hummed. Dessa did not once look at the back of Rook's head. And Wyck lay in the cart with his eyes shut and his ribs on fire and slept for the first time since the arch.
pauses.reason: Completed thought in Toren's internal monologue about the group's reaction.
